column2: plan-review voter and aggregator launches write `panel-prompt-sizes.tsv` beside outputs under `design_tmpdir` (e.g. `claude-vote-output.txt`, `aggregator-output.txt`), because logging derives the artifact from `path(args.output).parent`. specialists already write under `plan-review/round-n/`, but voter-dispatch lacks a round number and design outputs sit at the tmpdir root. committed design logs and publish tests expect `plan-review/round-<n>/panel-prompt-sizes.tsv`, so voter/aggregator rows miss that path, multi-round runs lose round attribution, and top-level tsvs may be committed incorrectly or omitted. the plan also introduces `panel_prompt_size_artifact_for_output()` while launcher instructions hardcode `output.parent`, bypassing centralized round-aware routing.

`agent_waterfall` launches many `launch-review` / `launch-claude-review` children in parallel per phase. each child appends to the same round-local `panel-prompt-sizes.tsv` before its long-running subprocess starts. the plan covers atomic header creation but not locked appends. interleaved concurrent header creation and row writes can duplicate headers, split or truncate rows, or produce malformed tsv that `measure_panel_cost` skips or mis-aggregates, corrupting committed implement/review/design metrics.

aggregator prompt-size logging has no explicit round-local artifact path and no agent-file attribution. launcher-only logging writes aggregator rows beside `aggregator-output.txt` at the design tmpdir root, not `plan-review/round-n`. the dispatch path forwards only `prompt_file` (aggregator-prompt.md), so `_review_launcher` sees no `args.agent_file` even though `review_aggregate` reads `agents/orchestrator-aggregator.md`. rows therefore miss the committed round-scoped tsv and cannot rank `agents/orchestrator-aggregator.md` as a panel-tier source file for `measure-panel-cost`.

python/larch/agents/_review_launcher.py:1178-1200; python/larch/agents/_claude_runner.py:450-552; python/larch/design/decompose.py:414-418; python/larch/design/plan_quality.py:754-769 [scope-reduction] broad launcher instrumentation would include non-panel callers. scenario: `agent launch-review` and `agent launch-claude-review` are reused by design decomposition and plan-autofix flows, so logging every call through these launchers can create `panel-prompt-sizes.tsv` outside reviewer, voter, aggregator, or implementer slots and pollute `measure-panel-cost` with non-panel prompt bytes

python/larch/design/plan_scout.py:468-473 [scope-reduction] global launch-review instrumentation has no explicit skip path for non-panel design launches. scenario: plan_scout and other design helpers use agent launch-review outside the panel-tier scope; if the launcher always writes output-parent panel-prompt-sizes.tsv, committed design logs and measure-panel-cost can include scout/autofix/decompose rows as panel cost.

python/larch/review/plan_review_panel.py:444-445,909-911; python/larch/review/review_aggregate.py:847-869; plan approach/_review_launcher sections [scope-reduction] design plan-review voter and aggregator rows will miss the per-round committed tsv. scenario: the plan commits design metrics only under `plan-review/round-<n>/panel-prompt-sizes.tsv` and warns against top-level-only placement. `dispatch_panel` writes specialist outputs under `round_dir`, but voters use `design / policies[...].output_name` at `$design_tmpdir` root (`plan_review_panel.py:909-911`), and aggregation keeps `aggregator-prompt.md` / `aggregator-output.txt` at `review_tmpdir` root even when `--round-dir` is passed (`review_aggregate.py:847-869`). launcher-side logging is pinned to `path(args.output).parent / "panel-prompt-sizes.tsv"`, so voters and aggregators append to `$design_tmpdir/panel-prompt-sizes.tsv`, not the round artifact the publish test and `measure_panel_cost` path parsing target. issue acceptance requires per-slot sizes across the design panel, not specialists only.

the plan wires panel prompt-size logging for design plan-review (`plan_review_panel.py`, plan-mode `review_aggregate.py`) but omits `/implement` step 5 and standalone `/review` panel dispatch entrypoints. `review_dispatch_panel.py` and `agent_voters.py` call `agent dispatch-waterfall` without setting `larch_panel_*` (or equivalent cli flags such as `--panel-artifact-dir`). because `_panel_logging_enabled()` requires a non-empty `larch_panel_slot`, specialist and voter slots launched through these paths will not write `panel-prompt-sizes.tsv` rows. acceptance requires per-slot prompt sizes for `/implement` step 5 and `/review` panels; without explicit opt-in wiring at these producers, committed run logs can stay empty except on fixtures that inject panel env manually. any default site heuristic in `agent_waterfall` risks falsely instrumenting out-of-scope callers such as `decompose.py`.

the plan updates `coder_runner.py` to append implementer prompt-size rows only when `larch_panel_slot` is already set, but no listed file sets panel env before `apply_findings_with_coder`. that path composes `coder-prompt.md` in-process during `/implement` step 5 and `/review` fix application; it uses `run-external-agent`, not `launch-review`, so `_review_launcher` never runs. with helper gating requiring `larch_panel_slot`, `append_panel_prompt_size` can skip every `review.fix_coder` prompt unless unrelated parent env happens to be set. issue scope and acceptance require implementer slot coverage alongside specialist, voter, and aggregator slots.

the plan sets aggregator panel env (`larch_panel_slot`, `larch_panel_source_agent_file=agents/orchestrator-aggregator.md`, artifact dir) only when `input_mode=plan` (and often only with `--round-dir`). `/implement` step 5 and `/review` invoke `aggregate-findings` with default `input_mode=code` and call `dispatch-waterfall` at `review_aggregate.py` without passing panel env into `subprocess.run`. code-review aggregator prompts therefore go unmeasured or lose `agents/orchestrator-aggregator.md` attribution, falling into generated or no-agent buckets. that understates aggregator panel cost in committed logs and prevents `measure-panel-cost` from ranking a required panel-tier source file.
